advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate that each slot config value is a Mapping and raise a typed LLMConfigError (naming the offending class) when it is not, instead of letting `raw.get(...)` raise AttributeError.
evidence: 134: def _parse_slot(name: str, raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ClassSlot:
135:     _reject_api_key(raw, what=f"the '{name}' class slot")
137:     model = raw.get("model") or _DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS[name]

parse_class_slots docstring at line 159 promises: 'Raises :class:`LLMConfigError` for an unknown class name, an ``api_key`` ... or a nested ``fallback``' — a non-mapping slot value falls outside that typed-error contract and surfaces as AttributeError
advisory.finding: A model-class slot whose config value is not a mapping (e.g. TOML `frontier = "gpt-4o"` instead of `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes.frontier]`) crashes with an untyped AttributeError instead of the typed LLMConfigError the parser promises for bad config. `_parse_slot` calls `_reject_api_key(raw, ...)` (`"api_key" in raw` succeeds harmlessly on a str) then `raw.get("model")`, which raises AttributeError on a str/non-Mapping.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_parse_slot`, guard `if not isinstance(raw, Mapping): raise LLMConfigError(f"the '{name}' class slot must be a table, not {type(raw).__name__}")` before the api_key check.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate that `fallback` is a list and each entry is a Mapping, raising a typed LLMConfigError otherwise, before parsing fallback entries.
evidence: 149:     fallback_raw = raw.get("fallback") or []
150:     fallback = tuple(_parse_fallback_entry(entry) for entry in fallback_raw)
69: def _parse_fallback_entry(raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> FallbackTarget:
76:     model = raw.get("model")  # AttributeError if entry is a str/non-Mapping
A string `fallback` value would be iterated char-by-char; a non-iterable (int) would TypeError at the comprehension — neither is the promised typed error
advisory.finding: A `fallback` value that is not a list, or a fallback list element that is not a mapping (e.g. `fallback = ["gpt-4o"]`, a very natural mistake), crashes with an untyped TypeError/AttributeError rather than a typed LLMConfigError. `fallback_raw = raw.get("fallback") or []` is iterated directly and each entry is passed to `_parse_fallback_entry`, which does `"api_key" in raw` then `raw.get("model")` — the latter raises AttributeError on a str element.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard `fb = raw.get("fallback") or []; if not isinstance(fb, list): raise LLMConfigError(...)`, and in `_parse_fallback_entry` raise LLMConfigError when the entry is not a Mapping.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Reject unknown/extra keys on class slots and fallback entries (closed schema) so credentials cannot be smuggled in under a key other than the literal `api_key`.
evidence: `def _reject_api_key(...): ... if "api_key" in raw:` (model_classes.py:63-66) — the guard keys on the single literal string `api_key` only.

`_parse_slot` (model_classes.py:134-152) reads only model/provider/endpoint/fallback and never rejects other keys present in `raw`; `_parse_fallback_entry` (model_classes.py:69-79) likewise rejects only `api_key` and `fallback`.

`parse_class_slots` rejects unknown CLASS names (`unknown = sorted(set(table) - set(CLASS_NAMES))`, model_classes.py:163-165) but performs NO unknown-FIELD rejection inside a slot/entry, so the slot mapping is not a closed schema.

Reachability: the ticket frames api_key rejection as the secrets boundary because 'LiteLLM puts api_key inline in litellm_params and copying that would put a credential in a committed file' (test_model_classes.py). A LiteLLM params block also carries other credential-bearing keys (e.g. aws_secret_access_key, api_base), which this allowlist-less parser would accept into a committed config table.

The raw leaked-secret STRING itself is owned by the deterministic secret-detection (gitleaks) criterion; this finding is the incomplete-validation / non-closed-schema gap in the safety check, not the token detection.
dropped.finding: The api_key secrets-boundary check (`_reject_api_key`) matches only the exact key `"api_key"`, and neither slot nor fallback-entry parsing rejects other/unknown field keys — so a credential committed under any differently-named key (e.g. `aws_secret_access_key`, `api_base` with an embedded token, `extra_headers`) is silently accepted, defeating the boundary this check exists to enforce.
scenarios: An operator adapts a LiteLLM `litellm_params` block into `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]`, keeping a credential key that is not literally named `api_key` (e.g. `aws_secret_access_key`); the parser accepts it and the credential lands in a committed pyproject/rebar.toml.
dropped.suggested_fix: Make the slot and fallback-entry schemas closed: after removing the known fields (model/provider/endpoint[/fallback]), raise `LLMConfigError` on any remaining key (without echoing its value), rather than only special-casing the literal `api_key`.
